D.t: Tina Kotek leads by 8.8 in the forecast and wins 92% of simulations. The cushion is about 180,789 votes; a one point swing is about 10,307 voters changing sides.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between D +0.9 and D +16.5. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.
The polls page average is R +0.7. Your best recent poll is DHM Research for The Oregonian at D +1.9; your worst is DHM Research/Oregon Public Broadcasting at R +1.7. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Multnomah, a projected net 246,102 votes; Washington, a projected net 76,418 votes; Lane, a projected net 37,349 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Clackamas, D +1.2, 10.8% of the vote; Marion, R +11.4, 7.0% of the vote; Deschutes, D +3.9, 5.5% of the vote; Clatsop, D +6.7, 1.0% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Tina Kotek runs furthest behind in Umatilla, Klamath, Douglas. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 86% of voters, 50 to 46, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.29 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 75% of voters, 54 to 42, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.77 points; Voters who find daily costs hard to afford, 62% of voters, 56 to 41, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.08 points.
The forecast's worst groups for Tina Kotek: Immigration voters 22 to 75, Small counties 36 to 60, Midsize counties 39 to 58. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
